# Edge

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

The fleet layer for a [Multisite](/docs/extensions/multisite): several servers (edges) share one set of instances, any edge accepts
any request, and a request for an instance another edge runs is forwarded there over the private network. Works with
either runtime provider, [pocker](/docs/extensions/pocker) or [docker](/docs/extensions/docker).

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Edge is built into `pocketone`. It turns on in host mode (a `multisite` section in `pocketone.yaml`) when the file has an
`edges` section, or a `mothership` section ([Mothership](/docs/extensions/mothership)), which lists the edges too.

In your own Go build, give the host a router as its forward hook:

```go
edges, err := edge.FromSection(log) // the `edges` section; nil when there is none
if edges != nil {
	opts.Forward = edge.NewRouter(edge.RouterConfig{Edges: edges, Logger: log}).Forward
}
h, err := multisite.FromConfig(opts)
```

The module is `pocketone.dev/ext/edge`.

## Configure

The `edges` section names this edge and lists the others (keys below):

```yaml
edges:
  self: lax-1
  list:
    - { id: sgp-1, internal_url: "http://10.88.0.4:8080", region: sgp }
server:
  plain: [":8080"]   # where the other edges reach this one (their internal_url for it)
```

Each entry needs `id` and `internal_url`. An instance another edge runs names its owner in `remote`:

```yaml
instances:
  - id: shop
    hosts: [shop.example.com]
    remote: edge:@sgp-1     # also accepted: edge:sgp-1, or sgp-1
```

Without a mothership, instances come from the instances file. With one, instances and edges both come from it; a
fixed `edges.list` entry wins over the mothership's for the same edge.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `edges:`

The fleet: this edge's id and a fixed list of the other edges (id, internal_url, region).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `self` | string |  | This edge's id, such as lax-1. |
| `list` | list of object |  | The other edges: id, internal_url (where this edge reaches it) and optional region. |

## Use

There's nothing to run by hand. A load balancer sends visitors to any edge, and each request ends up on the edge that
runs its instance:

- **Owner healthy:** the request is forwarded to its `internal_url`, with the original hostname. An edge is healthy
  when its source heard from it in the last 30 seconds, or else when it answers `/.well-known/health` (an edge the
  source marks offline never is).
- **Owner briefly unreachable but healthy:** requests are held and retried every 250 ms until it answers. Only
  requests without a body (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) are replayed after a failed connection.
- **Owner down or unknown:** a 503 with `Retry-After: 10`, at once.
- **Never bounced:** a request another edge already forwarded is never forwarded again; it gets a 421.
- **CORS:** for an instance with `access.cors_origins`, the entry edge answers preflights and sets the only
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` the browser sees.
- **Headers:** where both edges set the same header (such as the firewall's rate-limit headers), the owner's wins.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](/docs/extensions/multisite) | Edge fills the host's forward hook for instances with `remote` set. |
| [Pocker](/docs/extensions/pocker), [Docker](/docs/extensions/docker) | Either runs the instances this edge owns; an app already running here stops when its instance moves to another edge. |
| [Firewall](/docs/extensions/firewall) | The entry edge checks the peer and the instance's rate limits before forwarding. |
| [Mothership](/docs/extensions/mothership) | Its mirror is an edge source: it follows the mothership's list of edges and their heartbeats. |

### Building on Edge

- **Edge sources.** Implement `edge.EdgeSource` (`Self`, `Resolve`, `Edges`) to say where the other edges are; add
  `Run` (`edge.Runner`) for background work. `YAMLProvider` is the `edges.list` one; `MultiProvider` combines several,
  the first to resolve an instance's `remote` winning.
- **Router.** `edge.NewRouter(edge.RouterConfig{...})` takes the health path, healthy window, retry interval and the
  503 and 421 messages. Plug `Router.Forward` into `multisite.Host.Forward`.
- **Timing.** `edge.WithMark(ctx)` records which edge a request was forwarded to and when, e.g. for Server-Timing.

## Example

Edge has no example program of its own. The stock binary wires it up in
[`examples/pocketone/multi.go`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/examples/pocketone/multi.go), together with the mothership's edge list.
